enrollee_supplies_subject_disabled.title: Enrollee-Supplied Subject Disabled
enrollee_supplies_subject_disabled.description: Interpreted-secure boolean: true when the CA builds the certificate Subject/SAN from a trusted directory/identity source and a low-privileged requester CANNOT dictate identity (CT_FLAG_SUBJECT_REQUIRE_DIRECTORY_PATH set; AD CS CT_FLAG_ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT clear; EJBCA 'Allow Subject DN Override by CSR' disabled). False (insecure) when the requester may supply an arbitrary Subject/SAN/UPN — the ESC1 root cause.

template_grants_authentication_eku.title: Enrollee Template Grants Authentication EKU
template_grants_authentication_eku.description: Interpreted boolean: true when an enrollee-reachable template grants an authentication-capable EKU (Client Authentication 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.2, PKINIT Client Auth 1.3.6.1.5.2.3.4, or Smart Card Logon 1.3.6.1.4.1.311.20.2.2). Modeled as an interpreted boolean (not has_element on an EKU OID array) to stay polarity-safe. Combined with requester-supplied subject and no approval this turns a SAN into domain authentication (ESC1).

enrollee_supplied_san_requires_approval.title: Enrollee-Supplied SAN Requires Manager Approval
enrollee_supplied_san_requires_approval.description: Interpreted boolean: true when issuance for any template allowing requester-supplied subject/SAN (or carrying an auth/SubCA/enrollment-agent EKU) is held pending a Certificate Manager approval or required RA signature (AD CS CT_FLAG_PEND_ALL_REQUESTS / msPKI-RA-Signature). False (insecure) when such requests auto-issue with no manager approval — the compensating control that neutralises ESC1 is absent.

any_purpose_or_subca_eku_enrollable.title: Any-Purpose / Sub-CA EKU Enrollable
any_purpose_or_subca_eku_enrollable.description: Interpreted boolean: true when a low-privilege-enrollable template grants the Any Purpose EKU (2.5.29.37.0) or carries no EKU at all (subordinate-CA capable), yielding a certificate usable for any purpose including authentication or sub-CA creation (ESC2). Modeled as an interpreted boolean so the all-secure baseline (scoped purpose-specific EKUs) does not fire.

ca_wide_san_attribute_flag_disabled.title: CA-Wide SAN Attribute Flag Disabled
ca_wide_san_attribute_flag_disabled.description: Interpreted-secure boolean: TRUE when the CA-wide 'allow user-defined SAN in request attribute' policy flag is DISABLED (AD CS: EDITF_ATTRIBUTESUBJECTALTNAME2 absent from policy\EditFlags; generic CA: no global 'allow SAN/Subject override via request attribute'). FALSE (ESC6) means any request may carry an attacker-supplied SAN, globally re-enabling ESC1-style impersonation across every template regardless of per-template hardening.

manage_ca_rights_restricted.title: ManageCA Rights Restricted to Tier-0
manage_ca_rights_restricted.description: Interpreted-secure boolean: TRUE when CA-management rights (ManageCA / 'CA administrator' role) are restricted to dedicated Tier-0 admin accounts and withheld from broad or unprivileged principals (Authenticated Users, Domain Users), so the CA-wide SAN policy flag cannot be silently re-flipped by the subject it governs. FALSE (ESC7) means a broad/low-priv holder can flip EDITF_ATTRIBUTESUBJECTALTNAME2 at will, voiding every per-template control.

name_constraints_enforced.title: Name Constraints Enforced on Issuing CA
name_constraints_enforced.description: Interpreted-secure boolean: true when the issuing/subordinate CA certificate carries an X.509 NameConstraints extension (permitted/excluded DNS, IP, email, directory subtrees) scoping which identities it may ever sign, bound to the org's owned namespaces. False = no NameConstraints, so the CA (or a stolen subordinate key) can mint certificates for ANY name, including domains it does not own.

path_length_constraint_set.title: Path-Length Constraint Set
path_length_constraint_set.description: Interpreted-secure boolean: true when the issuing CA certificate's BasicConstraints pathLenConstraint is set to bound how many further intermediate CAs may chain below it (pathLen=0 on a leaf issuing CA = no further sub-CAs). False = pathLen unset or over-large, letting the CA spawn rogue subordinate CAs. EJBCA does NOT validate path length at issuance, so this must be set deliberately.

offline_root_ca.title: Offline Root CA Hierarchy
offline_root_ca.description: Interpreted-secure boolean: true when the trust-anchor root (and policy CA) is kept OFFLINE and separated from online issuing/subordinate CAs. False = single online root issuing leaf certs (flat hierarchy) or issuing CA co-located with a domain controller / other Tier-0 roles, so a single compromise forges unlimited trust across namespaces. Secondary trigger amplifying the unconstrained-CA blast radius.

key_storage.title: CA Signing Key Custody Tier
key_storage.description: The custody tier of the CA signing key. Secure tiers are the HSM/KMS-backed values (hsm_fips_l3, hsm_fips_l2) where key theft from a disk image is worthless. Insecure tiers are 'software_exportable' (on-disk PEM / DPAPI exportable — any local admin exports it) and 'software_non_exportable' (still recoverable from a disk image, no FIPS hardware boundary). Subsumes the boolean 'signing_key_hsm_backed' as its finer-grained form. Maps to dossier config key 'ca_private_key_storage'.

ca_key_bundled_in_routine_backup.title: CA Key Bundled in Routine Backup
ca_key_bundled_in_routine_backup.description: Interpreted boolean: true when routine backups bundle an exportable CA signing-key PFX onto general backup infrastructure (full system-state / certutil -backup) rather than DB-only backups with the key PFX isolated under chain-of-custody. True means the key is reachable from shared backup systems and a brute-forceable PFX hands an attacker the whole PKI; this widens the no-HSM key-theft exposure. Secure value: false; fires on true.

http_enrollment_endpoint_exposed.title: HTTP Enrollment Endpoint Exposed
http_enrollment_endpoint_exposed.description: Interpreted boolean: true when an HTTP-based enrollment endpoint (AD CS Web Enrollment /certsrv, CES/CEP, or NDES /CertSrv/mscep) is reachable on this CA. The relay attack surface exists only when such an HTTP endpoint is present; if web enrollment is removed entirely the ESC8 vector is closed. Fires is_true; secure value is false (endpoint removed/absent).

web_enrollment_https_enforced.title: Web Enrollment HTTPS-Only Enforced
web_enrollment_https_enforced.description: Interpreted boolean: true when the web-enrollment / CES-CEP / NDES endpoints are served HTTPS-only (plain HTTP bindings removed). When HTTP is accepted, coerced NTLM authentication can be relayed over an unprotected channel to obtain an authentication-capable certificate for the victim machine (AD CS ESC8). Fires is_false; secure value is true (HTTPS-only).

extended_protection_for_authentication_e.title: Extended Protection for Authentication Required
extended_protection_for_authentication_e.description: Interpreted boolean: true when IIS Extended Protection for Authentication (EPA / channel binding) is set to Required on the Windows Authentication of the enrollment endpoints. EPA binds the authentication to the TLS channel, defeating cross-protocol NTLM relay to the enrollment endpoint (ESC8). Fires is_false; secure value is true (EPA Required).

ntlm_authentication_disabled_on_enrollme.title: NTLM Disabled on Enrollment Endpoint
ntlm_authentication_disabled_on_enrollme.description: Interpreted boolean: true when NTLM is disabled on the HTTP enrollment endpoints (Kerberos/negotiate-only), so coerced NTLM auth cannot be relayed there at all. Disabling NTLM removes the relayed credential the ESC8 chain depends on. Fires is_false; secure value is true (NTLM disabled).

manage_certificates_rights_restricted.title: ManageCertificates Rights Restricted
manage_certificates_rights_restricted.description: Interpreted-secure boolean: true when the ManageCertificates (Certificate Manager) issuance/approval permission is restricted to dedicated, vetted certificate-officer accounts and is not held by broad or unprivileged principals. False when granted broadly — a holder can approve their own pending request, bypassing manager approval (ESC7).

ca_admin_mfa_enforced.title: MFA Enforced for CA Admin Access
ca_admin_mfa_enforced.description: Interpreted-secure boolean: true when MFA / smart-card is enforced for interactive CA management access and CA admins use dedicated alternate (not daily-driver) accounts. False when CA console access is password-only with no MFA, easing credential abuse on ManageCA/ManageCertificates holders.

role_separation_enabled.title: Common-Criteria Role Separation Enabled
role_separation_enabled.description: Interpreted-secure boolean: true when Common-Criteria role separation is enforced so no single identity holds both ManageCA and ManageCertificates (admin vs issuer vs auditor vs backup duties split) and the setting is change-monitored. False when role separation is off/unset — one account both weakens policy and approves issuance.

template_acls_hardened.title: Certificate-Template ACLs Hardened
template_acls_hardened.description: Interpreted-secure boolean: true when ACLs on certificate-template AD objects limit Write/WriteDacl/WriteProperty/FullControl to Domain Admins / dedicated PKI-admin groups, with no such rights for unprivileged principals. False when a non-Tier-0 principal holds WriteDacl/WriteProperty/FullControl on a template — they can reconfigure a benign template into an ESC1 template (ESC4).

pki_object_acls_hardened.title: PKI Infrastructure-Object ACLs Hardened
pki_object_acls_hardened.description: Interpreted-secure boolean: true when ACLs on PKI infrastructure objects (CA computer object, NTAuthCertificates, CN=Public Key Services PKI containers) are Tier-0-protected with no Write/FullControl for unprivileged principals. False when dangerous ACLs on PKI objects/NTAuth are granted to non-Tier-0 principals — enabling RBCD or NTAuth poisoning to compromise the CA/forest (ESC5).

crl_or_ocsp_configured.title: CRL or OCSP Revocation Configured
crl_or_ocsp_configured.description: Interpreted-secure boolean: true when the CA publishes a working revocation method — a CRL and/or OCSP responder — with CDP/AIA URLs embedded in issued certificates. Fires when no revocation mechanism is configured at all, so a compromised or mis-issued certificate stays trusted until natural expiry with no kill-switch.

crl_distribution_point_reachable.title: CRL/AIA Distribution Point Reachable
crl_distribution_point_reachable.description: Interpreted-secure boolean: true when the CDP/AIA URLs embedded in issued certificates are actually reachable by relying parties so CRL/OCSP fetches succeed. Fires when the distribution point is unreachable (dead URL, network-isolated, DNS failure) — relying parties silently fall open and revocation is unenforced even though a method is nominally configured.

crl_response_fresh.title: CRL / OCSP Response Fresh
crl_response_fresh.description: Interpreted-secure boolean: true when the published CRL's nextUpdate is in the future (not expired) and OCSP responses carry a short next-update — i.e. revocation data is current. Fires when the CRL is stale/expired, in which case relying parties may treat it as invalid and fall open, leaving revoked certificates trusted.

max_leaf_validity_days.title: Maximum Leaf Certificate Validity (Days)
max_leaf_validity_days.description: The maximum validity period (in days) the CA grants to leaf certificates. HIGH_IS_INSECURE: an over-long lifetime widens the window a compromised or mis-issued certificate stays usable before its only backstop (natural expiry) kicks in — most damaging precisely when revocation is missing or stale. Fires when greater than 397 days (the CA/Browser Forum public-TLS leaf ceiling); secure is a short bounded value.

requester_validity_override_disabled.title: Requester Validity Override Disabled
requester_validity_override_disabled.description: Interpreted-secure boolean: true when the requester CANNOT dictate certificate lifetime (EJBCA 'Allow Validity Override' disabled, or the AD CS template not honouring a requester-supplied notAfter). Fires when validity override is enabled, letting an enrollee demand an arbitrary (over-long) lifetime, widening the trusted window for a compromised cert beyond the CA's intended bound.

signing_hash_algorithm.title: CA Signing Hash Algorithm
signing_hash_algorithm.description: Hash algorithm the CA uses in its certificate signatures. SHA-256+ is the modern floor; sha1/md5 are deprecated and produce forgeable signatures, undermining the integrity of every certificate the CA signs. Fires on in[sha1, md5].

ca_key_algorithm_strength.title: CA Signing Key Algorithm Strength
ca_key_algorithm_strength.description: The CA signing key's algorithm and strength. Floors are RSA >= 2048 (3072+ for long-lived roots) or P-256/P-384 ECDSA. rsa_1024 (or smaller) is below the current floor and a brute-forcible/forgeable signing key undermines the entire chain. Fires on in[rsa_1024, rsa_512].

issuance_audit_logging_enabled.title: Issuance Audit Logging Enabled
issuance_audit_logging_enabled.description: Interpreted-secure boolean: true when the CA records every certificate issuance, revocation, and template change to an audit log across all event categories (AD CS: certutil -getreg CA\AuditFilter = 127 AND the OS 'Audit object access' policy enabled Success/Failure). Fires when false/partial — rogue-certificate minting, the goal of every AD CS ESC primitive, becomes invisible.

audit_logs_forwarded_to_siem.title: Audit Logs Forwarded to SIEM
audit_logs_forwarded_to_siem.description: Interpreted-secure boolean: true when CA issuance/revocation/admin audit events are centrally retained by forwarding to a SIEM rather than left only in the local host event log (where they can be cleared or lost on host compromise). Fires when false — locally-only logs are non-attributable and unavailable for PKI-abuse detection across the estate.

admin_action_logging_enabled.title: Admin Action Logging Enabled
admin_action_logging_enabled.description: Interpreted-secure boolean: true when CA administrative actions — template changes, CA security/ACL edits, policy-flag changes (e.g. EDITF_ATTRIBUTESUBJECTALTNAME2), role-separation toggles — are audited and attributable to individual operators. Fires when false: a config-weakening admin action that enables an ESC primitive leaves no attributable trace.

audit_logs_tamper_protected.title: Audit Logs Tamper-Protected
audit_logs_tamper_protected.description: Interpreted-secure boolean: true when CA audit logs are tamper-resistant — write-once / off-host retained so a local administrator (or attacker who minted a rogue cert) cannot delete or edit the issuance record to cover the abuse. Fires when false: even enabled logs are unreliable evidence because they can be cleared by the very subject they would incriminate.
